note: Wren Phonics — Fast Track guide (b410, 2026-10-08), built from research §1D (catch-up for older pupils as an idea, common SSP practice) and the Reading Framework (July 2023) p.68-75/p.66, in Wren's own words. provenance: Wren original, b410, 2026-10-08.
who: Pupils in Year 2 or above (roughly age 7+) who are not yet reading through phonic decoding to an age-appropriate standard — commonly a reading age of 8 or below (Reading Framework, July 2023, p.68-75). This includes a pupil who did not meet the Phonics Screening Check standard and is retaking it, and any older pupil, new to the setting or not, who needs systematic phonics teaching rather than a different reading strategy.
same_programme: Fast Track teaches the exact same GPC sequence, in the exact same order, as the main Wren Phonics schedule — it is a faster PACE through the same progression, never a different or simplified programme (Reading Framework guidance is explicit that pupils needing extra support should get more of the same systematic phonics, not a substitute).
start_point: Never start at week one by default. Place every pupil with the Fast Track placement check first and start teaching at the point it actually shows — a pupil who already knows most Phase 2 and 3 sounds securely should not sit through them again from scratch.
pace: The core schedule spreads its 47 teaching weeks across 12 half-terms with a dedicated settling week and 24 consolidation/review weeks built in around them. Fast Track pupils are older and already have the skills those surrounding weeks exist to build through review and consolidation (Phase 1, the Reception settling week) — so Fast Track drops them by design and pairs the remaining teaching weeks two at a time into 24 faster-paced "Fast Track weeks" (grouped into 12 stages of 2, one stage per half-term of the core schedule), covering the same full GPC progression in roughly a third of the time. A short revisit-and-review slot opens every Fast Track week instead of whole separate consolidation weeks.
timing: "A few months" of intensive, daily, time-limited teaching, then stop and reassess (Reading Framework p.68-75) — Fast Track is not meant to run open-ended for a whole school year. Review progress at the end of every stage (every 2 Fast Track weeks) and recalculate whether the pupil can now move to normal-pace teaching, needs another stage at Fast Track pace, or needs a different kind of support altogether.
group_size: Small group or 1:1, daily, in a consistent place and time — the Reading Framework's own description of effective extra provision (p.66) applies here too.
age_appropriate_materials: Fast Track materials deliberately drop the six Wren Phonics cast characters (Pip, Ned, Olive, Moss, Fig, Nell) and the nursery/wren-bird motifs used in the main programme's youngest-child materials — plain word and sentence lists only, with the technical pronunciation and formation guidance kept (nothing about how a sound is taught changes, only the picture-book framing around it; the per-grapheme mnemonic pictures and actions are a separate, unrelated set and are also dropped here for the same reason). The goal is a resource an 8 to 11-year-old can use without it looking like it was made for a much younger child.
monitoring: Keep a progress record per pupil (see the separate progress-record template) updated at least at the end of every stage. A pupil who is not moving through stages at the expected faster pace needs a different conversation — about whether Fast Track is the right response at all, not just more of it.
